layer_at_fault_line: No finding in the report is contradicted by the document, and no mismarking traceable to the skill's own wording was found; nothing here calls for a fault attribution.
quotes:
test_swap/test_poke (numeric estimates — one half only, no specific neighbour named): "The text itself says the conclusion survives being off by 'several orders of magnitude.' Swap the numbers, nothing moves."

test_reverse (names which of the two questions is answered): "The indifference-principle step is careful to stay on the identification side ('what can we tell from what we see') rather than sliding into a production claim, and Section V spends real effort separating it from the Doomsday argument's different (and more contested) premise — a random sample across all time."

test_hunt: "'We have no information that our own experience is any more or less likely to be simulated' is the trigger for the indifference principle, but there is no stated gauge for what would count as such information."

pairs_that_pull sent here because neither side is a part label from Section 2/3's list: "Bostrom notes the tension himself: vast, cheap computation pushes toward disjunct (3) being forced, while posthuman ethical sophistication is one route to disjunct (2) (a ban on ancestor-simulations). He doesn't resolve which wins — he reports it as an open pull, which is honest rather than hidden."

rivals_built sent here because the rival is only named, not built (no distinguishing change is offered, nor a plain statement that none exists): "Unusually, the argument's own structure supplies its strongest rivals: (1) and (2) are the rival explanations to (3), stated by the author rather than smuggled in or dismissed."
